questions.unit: Unit 2: Probability, Random Variables, and Probability Distributions
questions.prompt: A nonnegative integer random variable X can equal 0, 1, 2, or 3. Use the identity E(X) = P(X ≥ 1) + P(X ≥ 2) + P(X ≥ 3). If these three probabilities are 0.80, 0.50, and 0.20, respectively, what is E(X)?
questions.explanation: Apply the supplied tail-sum identity: E(X) = 0.80 + 0.50 + 0.20 = 1.50.

questions.unit: Unit 1: Exploring One-Variable Data and Collecting Data
questions.prompt: In a boxplot, the median is close to Q1, and the upper half of the box and upper whisker are much longer than their lower counterparts. Which statement is most appropriate?

choices.A: The display suggests right skew, although a boxplot does not show every feature of the distribution.
choices.B: The distribution must be exactly normal because the median lies inside the box.
choices.C: The mean must equal Q3 because the upper whisker is long.
choices.D: The display proves that more than 75% of observations are above the median.

questions.correctAnswerText: The display suggests right skew, although a boxplot does not show every feature of the distribution.
questions.explanation: Greater spread above the median and a longer upper whisker are consistent with a longer right tail. A boxplot gives limited shape information, so it suggests rather than proves a particular distributional form.

questions.unit: Unit 4: Inference for Quantitative Data: Means
questions.prompt: Two two-sided t-tests have the same value |t| = 2.1. Test 1 has df = 5, and test 2 has df = 50. Which statement is correct about their p-values?

choices.A: Test 1 has the smaller p-value because fewer observations create stronger evidence.
choices.B: The p-values are equal because the t statistics have equal magnitudes.
choices.C: Test 2 has p-value 0 because df is large.
choices.D: Test 2 has the smaller p-value because the t distribution has lighter tails at the larger degrees of freedom.

questions.correctAnswerText: Test 2 has the smaller p-value because the t distribution has lighter tails at the larger degrees of freedom.
questions.explanation: With the same |t|, a t distribution with more degrees of freedom places less probability in the two tails beyond that magnitude. Its p-value is therefore smaller, though not zero.

questions.unit: Unit 3: Inference for Categorical Data: Proportions
questions.prompt: A company compares independent random samples processed by an automated method and a manual method. It seeks evidence that the automated method has a higher population on-time proportion. Which hypotheses are appropriate?

choices.A: H0: p_auto > p_manual; Ha: p_auto = p_manual
choices.B: H0: p_auto = p_manual; Ha: p_auto > p_manual
choices.C: H0: p̂_auto = p̂_manual; Ha: p̂_auto > p̂_manual
choices.D: H0: p_auto = p_manual; Ha: p_auto ≠ p_manual

questions.correctAnswerText: H0: p_auto = p_manual; Ha: p_auto > p_manual
questions.explanation: Hypotheses use population proportions, equality is placed in H0, and “higher” determines a right-tailed alternative for p_auto − p_manual.

questions.unit: Unit 5: Regression Analysis
questions.prompt: A regression model predicts equipment energy use y from operating load x. At x = 8, the predicted energy use is 26 units, and the least-squares slope is 2.5. What is the intercept of the regression line?
questions.explanation: Substituting the fitted point into ŷ = b₀ + 2.5x gives 26 = b₀ + 2.5(8). Therefore b₀ = 26 − 20 = 6.

questions.unit: Unit 1: Exploring One-Variable Data and Collecting Data
questions.prompt: In an experiment comparing two visible physical-therapy programs, participants and therapists cannot be blinded. Which step would still help reduce outcome-assessment bias?

choices.A: Let each therapist score only participants who received that therapist's preferred program.
choices.B: Tell assessors which program is expected to work better.
choices.C: Allow participants to choose which assessor evaluates them.
choices.D: Have assessors who do not know treatment assignments evaluate the final mobility recordings.

questions.correctAnswerText: Have assessors who do not know treatment assignments evaluate the final mobility recordings.
questions.explanation: Blinding outcome assessors prevents knowledge of treatment from systematically influencing mobility scores, even when participants and treatment providers cannot be blinded.

questions.unit: Unit 2: Probability, Random Variables, and Probability Distributions
questions.prompt: A manufacturer wants to estimate the probability that an item fails an initial inspection while avoiding strong dependence among observations from the same production batch. Which plan is best?

choices.A: Randomly select many batches and inspect one randomly selected item from each selected batch.
choices.B: Inspect every item from one conveniently selected batch.
choices.C: Inspect the first item produced after each supervisor's lunch break.
choices.D: Ask supervisors to nominate items that appear likely to fail.

questions.correctAnswerText: Randomly select many batches and inspect one randomly selected item from each selected batch.
questions.explanation: Spreading observations across randomly selected batches and using one item per batch reduces within-batch dependence while giving batches and items a defined selection mechanism.

questions.unit: Unit 3: Inference for Categorical Data: Proportions
questions.prompt: A sample proportion is p̂ = 0.32, and its estimated standard error for a confidence interval is 0.020. Approximately what sample size produced this standard error?

questions.unit: Unit 1: Exploring One-Variable Data and Collecting Data
questions.prompt: Dataset A has standard deviation 2 meters. Dataset B measures the same type of quantity and has standard deviation 150 centimeters. Which dataset has greater spread as measured by standard deviation?

choices.A: Dataset B, because 150 is greater than 2
choices.B: The spreads are equal because both standard deviations are positive
choices.C: The comparison is impossible unless the means are equal
choices.D: Dataset A, because 2 meters equals 200 centimeters

questions.correctAnswerText: Dataset A, because 2 meters equals 200 centimeters
questions.explanation: Standard deviations must be expressed in common units before comparison. Dataset A's standard deviation is 200 centimeters, which exceeds 150 centimeters.

questions.unit: Unit 4: Inference for Quantitative Data: Means
questions.prompt: Employees are selected by a simple random sample from a company and then randomly assigned to one of two break schedules. A confidence interval for the mean treatment effect on completed tasks is entirely positive. Which scope statement is justified?

choices.A: The result is causal but applies only to the particular employees observed, despite the random sample.
choices.B: The result generalizes to all workers everywhere because assignment was random.
choices.C: The design supports a causal conclusion for, and generalization to, the company's employee population represented by the sampling frame.
choices.D: The design supports association only because confidence intervals cannot be used with experiments.

questions.correctAnswerText: The design supports a causal conclusion for, and generalization to, the company's employee population represented by the sampling frame.
questions.explanation: Random assignment supports causation, and the simple random sample supports generalization to the employee population covered by the sampling frame.

questions.unit: Unit 5: Regression Analysis
questions.prompt: A study assigns participants different numerical exercise durations and measures resting heart rate before and after the program. The goal is to model how heart-rate change is associated with assigned exercise duration. Which formulation is appropriate?

choices.A: For each participant, use assigned exercise duration as x and after-minus-before heart-rate change as y.
choices.B: Use participant identity as x and assigned duration as y.
choices.C: Use one overall mean duration as x and one overall mean heart rate as y.
choices.D: Use before-program heart rate as both x and y.

questions.correctAnswerText: For each participant, use assigned exercise duration as x and after-minus-before heart-rate change as y.
questions.explanation: The quantitative explanatory value and quantitative response change must remain paired for each participant. A regression can then describe how mean heart-rate change varies with assigned duration.

questions.unit: Unit 2: Probability, Random Variables, and Probability Distributions
questions.prompt: Two mutually exclusive causes account for an alarm. The probability of cause A is 0.30 and the probability of cause B is 0.20. Given that the alarm was caused by either A or B, what is the probability that A was the cause?
questions.explanation: Because A and B are mutually exclusive, P(A | A or B) = P(A)/[P(A) + P(B)] = 0.30/0.50 = 0.60.

questions.unit: Unit 3: Inference for Categorical Data: Proportions
questions.prompt: A retailer wants to estimate the proportion of item-location-time combinations for which a product is out of stock. Which plan best defines a probability sample from the target population?

choices.A: Check products that customers report as unavailable.
choices.B: Inspect only the highest-selling product at noon each day.
choices.C: Randomly select combinations from a complete list of products, store locations, and eligible time blocks, then record stock status.
choices.D: Ask store managers to choose combinations that seem typical.

questions.correctAnswerText: Randomly select combinations from a complete list of products, store locations, and eligible time blocks, then record stock status.
questions.explanation: The target observational unit is an item-location-time combination. Randomly sampling from a complete list gives each such combination a defined chance of selection.

questions.unit: Unit 1: Exploring One-Variable Data and Collecting Data
questions.prompt: A quantitative dataset has sample variance 4. A transformed variable is defined by y = −3x + 10. What is the sample variance of y?
questions.explanation: Adding 10 does not affect variance, while multiplying by −3 multiplies variance by (−3)² = 9. Thus s_y² = 9(4) = 36.

questions.unit: Unit 4: Inference for Quantitative Data: Means
questions.prompt: For a random sample of days, a forecast error is defined as actual high temperature minus forecast high temperature. Which procedure addresses whether the forecasting method is unbiased on average?

choices.A: A two-proportion z-test comparing warm and cool days
choices.B: A one-sample t-test of H0: μ_error = 0 against Ha: μ_error ≠ 0
choices.C: A paired t-test pairing unrelated days from different months
choices.D: A two-sample t-test treating actual and forecast temperatures as independent groups

questions.correctAnswerText: A one-sample t-test of H0: μ_error = 0 against Ha: μ_error ≠ 0
questions.explanation: Each day yields one quantitative forecast error. Unbiasedness on average corresponds to a population mean error of zero, so a two-sided one-sample t-test is appropriate.

questions.unit: Unit 2: Probability, Random Variables, and Probability Distributions
questions.stimulus: Four maintenance tasks, labeled A, B, C, and D, are placed in a uniformly random order. All 24 possible task orders are equally likely.
questions.prompt: Four tasks A, B, C, and D are placed in a uniformly random order. What is the probability that task A is first?
questions.explanation: By symmetry, task A is equally likely to occupy any of the four positions, so P(A first) = 1/4.

questions.unit: Unit 2: Probability, Random Variables, and Probability Distributions
questions.stimulus: Four maintenance tasks, labeled A, B, C, and D, are placed in a uniformly random order. All 24 possible task orders are equally likely.
questions.prompt: Four tasks A, B, C, and D are placed in a uniformly random order. What is the probability that tasks A and B are adjacent, in either order?
questions.explanation: Treat A and B as one block. The block and the other two tasks can be ordered in 3! ways, and A and B can occur in either internal order, giving 2(3!) = 12 favorable orders among 4! = 24. Thus the probability is 1/2.

questions.unit: Unit 2: Probability, Random Variables, and Probability Distributions
questions.stimulus: Four maintenance tasks, labeled A, B, C, and D, are placed in a uniformly random order. All 24 possible task orders are equally likely.
questions.prompt: Four tasks A, B, C, and D are placed in a uniformly random order. Given that A is first, why is the conditional probability that B is second equal to 1/3?

choices.A: Three of the four tasks are equally likely to be first.
choices.B: There are three possible positions for A after the first position is filled.
choices.C: The events “A first” and “B second” are mutually exclusive.
choices.D: After A is fixed first, each of B, C, and D is equally likely to occupy the second position.

questions.correctAnswerText: After A is fixed first, each of B, C, and D is equally likely to occupy the second position.
questions.explanation: Conditioning on A first leaves three tasks randomly ordered in the remaining positions. Each is equally likely to be second, so P(B second | A first) = 1/3.

questions.unit: Unit 1: Exploring One-Variable Data and Collecting Data
questions.prompt: A city wants to sample pedestrians using a large downtown area over a full week. Which plan best spreads selection across both place and time?

choices.A: Interview people leaving the busiest station during Friday rush hour.
choices.B: Randomly select intersection-time blocks across the week, then use a fixed rule to sample pedestrians within each selected block.
choices.C: Ask volunteers at several intersections to complete an online form later.
choices.D: Follow one randomly chosen pedestrian and interview everyone that person meets.

questions.correctAnswerText: Randomly select intersection-time blocks across the week, then use a fixed rule to sample pedestrians within each selected block.
questions.explanation: Randomly selecting both locations and times spreads coverage across the target setting, and a prespecified within-block rule avoids interviewer convenience selection.

questions.unit: Unit 3: Inference for Categorical Data: Proportions
questions.prompt: In a two-proportion test, the observed difference is p̂₁ − p̂₂ = 0.12 and the null standard error is 0.04. What is the z statistic?
questions.explanation: The statistic is z = (observed difference − null difference)/SE₀ = (0.12 − 0)/0.04 = 3.00.

questions.unit: Unit 5: Regression Analysis
questions.prompt: Over twelve months, both cumulative advertising expenditure and cumulative sales have a very high positive correlation. Why should this correlation be interpreted cautiously?

choices.A: Correlation cannot be computed for variables measured in dollars.
choices.B: A positive correlation proves advertising has no effect on sales.
choices.C: Cumulative variables must always have correlation 0.
choices.D: Both cumulative totals tend to rise with time, so a shared time trend can create a strong association without establishing a causal effect.

questions.correctAnswerText: Both cumulative totals tend to rise with time, so a shared time trend can create a strong association without establishing a causal effect.
questions.explanation: A common upward time trend can produce a high correlation between cumulative variables even when the month-to-month relationship does not support a causal claim.

questions.unit: Unit 4: Inference for Quantitative Data: Means
questions.prompt: A confidence interval for μ₁ − μ₂ is (−3, 5). If 7 is added to every observation in population 1's sample and nothing is changed in population 2's sample, what is the corresponding interval after the transformation?
questions.explanation: Adding 7 to every observation in group 1 increases x̄₁ − x̄₂ and both interval endpoints by 7 while leaving the standard error unchanged. The new interval is (−3 + 7, 5 + 7) = (4, 12).

questions.unit: Unit 1: Exploring One-Variable Data and Collecting Data
questions.prompt: A packaging manager wants to compare the consistency of fill weights from two machines, not their typical fill levels. Which comparison most directly addresses the question?

choices.A: Compare only the two sample means.
choices.B: Compare measures of spread, such as the sample standard deviations or IQRs, for the two machines.
choices.C: Compare the names and ages of the machines.
choices.D: Combine all observations and calculate one overall median.

questions.correctAnswerText: Compare measures of spread, such as the sample standard deviations or IQRs, for the two machines.
questions.explanation: Consistency concerns variability rather than center. Standard deviation and IQR measure spread, whereas means compare typical levels.

questions.unit: Unit 2: Probability, Random Variables, and Probability Distributions
questions.prompt: Three children independently choose one of five equally likely colors. What is the probability that at least two children choose the same color?
questions.explanation: The complement is that all three choices differ. After any first color, the next two must choose different unused colors, giving probability (4/5)(3/5) = 12/25. Therefore the requested probability is 1 − 12/25 = 13/25.

questions.unit: Unit 3: Inference for Categorical Data: Proportions
questions.prompt: A test fails to reject H0, and the study had power only 0.25 at a scientifically meaningful alternative value. Which conclusion is most appropriate?

choices.A: H0 has a 0.75 probability of being true.
choices.B: The meaningful alternative has been ruled out.
choices.C: The result is inconclusive because a study with low power often fails to detect a meaningful departure from H0.
choices.D: The Type I error probability must be 0.75.

questions.correctAnswerText: The result is inconclusive because a study with low power often fails to detect a meaningful departure from H0.
questions.explanation: Power 0.25 means the test rejects only about 25% of the time at that meaningful alternative. A failure to reject from such a study provides weak evidence against that alternative.

questions.unit: Unit 1: Exploring One-Variable Data and Collecting Data
questions.prompt: A frequency table has values 0, 1, 2, and 3 with frequencies 2, 5, 6, and 2, respectively. What is the median of the 15 observations?
questions.explanation: With 15 observations, the median is the eighth ordered value. The first 2 values are 0 and the next 5 are 1, so positions 8 through 13 are 2; therefore the median is 2.

questions.unit: Unit 4: Inference for Quantitative Data: Means
questions.prompt: Researchers want to compare mean sound levels in two neighborhoods. Which plan best controls measurement differences while supporting population inference?

choices.A: Randomly select comparable location-time combinations in each neighborhood and use the same calibrated meter and protocol for every measurement.
choices.B: Measure the loudest location in neighborhood 1 at night and the quietest location in neighborhood 2 in the morning.
choices.C: Let residents submit sound readings from any phone app they choose.
choices.D: Use one meter in neighborhood 1 and a differently calibrated meter in neighborhood 2.

questions.correctAnswerText: Randomly select comparable location-time combinations in each neighborhood and use the same calibrated meter and protocol for every measurement.
questions.explanation: Random location-time selection supports population inference, and one calibrated instrument and protocol prevent measurement method from being confounded with neighborhood.

questions.unit: Unit 3: Inference for Categorical Data: Proportions
questions.prompt: Before collecting data, a researcher expects a population proportion near 0.04. What minimum sample size is needed so that the expected numbers of successes and failures are both at least 10?
questions.explanation: The expected success count requires 0.04n ≥ 10, so n ≥ 250. At n = 250, the expected failure count is 0.96(250) = 240, which also exceeds 10.

questions.unit: Unit 4: Inference for Quantitative Data: Means
questions.prompt: In a one-sample t-test, x̄, μ0, and n are held fixed while the sample standard deviation doubles. What happens to the t statistic?

choices.A: Its magnitude doubles.
choices.B: It increases by 2.
choices.C: Its magnitude is cut in half.
choices.D: It is unchanged.

questions.correctAnswerText: Its magnitude is cut in half.
questions.explanation: The statistic is t = (x̄ − μ0)/(s/√n). Doubling s doubles the denominator while leaving the numerator fixed, so the magnitude of t is halved.

questions.unit: Unit 3: Inference for Categorical Data: Proportions
questions.prompt: A researcher selects clusters of students and computes a confidence interval for a proportion as if all students were independently sampled. Students within the same cluster tend to respond similarly. Which assessment is best?

choices.A: The interval is automatically valid because the total number of students is large.
choices.B: Clustering makes the sample proportion equal the population proportion.
choices.C: The interval must be too wide because similar responses increase information.
choices.D: Ignoring within-cluster dependence can understate the standard error and make the interval too narrow.

questions.correctAnswerText: Ignoring within-cluster dependence can understate the standard error and make the interval too narrow.
questions.explanation: Similar responses within clusters provide less independent information than the same number of independently sampled students. An independence-based standard error can therefore be too small.

questions.unit: Unit 2: Probability, Random Variables, and Probability Distributions
questions.prompt: A simulation will estimate the probability that a sequence of 12 fair coin flips contains a run of at least 3 consecutive heads. What should be recorded from each simulated sequence?

choices.A: Whether the sequence contains at least one run of 3 or more consecutive heads
choices.B: The total number of heads, regardless of their order
choices.C: Only the result of the twelfth flip
choices.D: The number of heads among the first three positions only

questions.correctAnswerText: Whether the sequence contains at least one run of 3 or more consecutive heads
questions.explanation: Each simulated sequence should be classified according to the event of interest. The estimated probability is the proportion of sequences whose longest head run is at least 3.

questions.unit: Unit 3: Inference for Categorical Data: Proportions
questions.prompt: In a random sample of 400 observations, p̂ = 0.62. Using z* = 1.96, which is the approximate 95% confidence interval for p?

questions.unit: Unit 1: Exploring One-Variable Data and Collecting Data
questions.prompt: Researchers plan an observational study of screen use and later sleep duration among adolescents. Which plan is strongest for measuring an association while preserving temporal order?

choices.A: Ask volunteers once whether they think screens harm sleep.
choices.B: Select a probability sample, measure baseline screen use, then follow participants and record later sleep duration using a common protocol.
choices.C: Randomly assign adolescents to report either screen use or sleep, but not both.
choices.D: Select only adolescents already attending a sleep clinic.

questions.correctAnswerText: Select a probability sample, measure baseline screen use, then follow participants and record later sleep duration using a common protocol.
questions.explanation: A probability sample supports generalization, measuring screen use before later sleep preserves temporal order, and a common protocol improves measurement consistency. The observational design still does not by itself establish causation.

questions.unit: Unit 4: Inference for Quantitative Data: Means
questions.prompt: For an independent two-sample mean procedure, SE = √(s₁²/n₁ + s₂²/n₂). If n₁, s₁, and s₂ are held fixed while n₂ becomes extremely large, what happens to the standard error?

choices.A: It increases without bound.
choices.B: It approaches s₂/√n₂.
choices.C: It becomes exactly zero.
choices.D: It approaches s₁/√n₁ because uncertainty from sample 1 remains.

questions.correctAnswerText: It approaches s₁/√n₁ because uncertainty from sample 1 remains.
questions.explanation: As n₂ grows, s₂²/n₂ approaches zero, but the fixed contribution s₁²/n₁ remains. Therefore the total standard error approaches √(s₁²/n₁) = s₁/√n₁ rather than zero.

questions.unit: Unit 5: Regression Analysis
questions.stimulus: A store records x = hours since opening and y = customer wait time. Express-service customers, who mostly arrive later, form a band near 5 minutes; standard-service customers, who mostly arrive earlier, form a band near 20 minutes. Within each service type, the scatterplot shows little relationship between x and y. When both types are combined, the overall scatterplot slopes downward.
questions.prompt: Express customers mostly arrive later with waits near 5 minutes, while standard customers mostly arrive earlier with waits near 20 minutes. What direction should the combined correlation between hours since opening and wait time have?

choices.A: Negative
choices.B: Positive
choices.C: Exactly zero
choices.D: It cannot have a sign because service type is categorical.

questions.correctAnswerText: Negative
questions.explanation: Later observations are mostly express customers with low waits, while earlier observations are mostly standard customers with high waits. This arrangement produces a downward overall association and negative correlation.

questions.unit: Unit 5: Regression Analysis
questions.stimulus: A store records x = hours since opening and y = customer wait time. Express-service customers, who mostly arrive later, form a band near 5 minutes; standard-service customers, who mostly arrive earlier, form a band near 20 minutes. Within each service type, the scatterplot shows little relationship between x and y. When both types are combined, the overall scatterplot slopes downward.
questions.prompt: Within each service type, the scatterplot of hours since opening and wait time shows little relationship. Which description is most accurate?

choices.A: Both within-type correlations must be strongly negative.
choices.B: Each within-type correlation is likely near zero even though the combined correlation is negative.
choices.C: The combined correlation must equal the average of the two within-type correlations.
choices.D: Correlation cannot be computed within a service type.

questions.correctAnswerText: Each within-type correlation is likely near zero even though the combined correlation is negative.
questions.explanation: The stimulus states that wait time has little relationship with time inside either service band. The overall negative pattern is produced by the groups occupying different regions of the plot.

questions.unit: Unit 5: Regression Analysis
questions.stimulus: A store records x = hours since opening and y = customer wait time. Express-service customers, who mostly arrive later, form a band near 5 minutes; standard-service customers, who mostly arrive earlier, form a band near 20 minutes. Within each service type, the scatterplot shows little relationship between x and y. When both types are combined, the overall scatterplot slopes downward.
questions.prompt: The combined scatterplot shows a negative association between hours since opening and wait time, but each service type separately shows little association. Which conclusion is best?

choices.A: Wait time necessarily falls as the day progresses for both service types.
choices.B: Hours since opening causes customers to switch service types.
choices.C: Service type is associated with both arrival time and wait time, so the combined negative association should not be interpreted as a common within-type trend.
choices.D: A regression line fitted to all customers eliminates the need to examine groups.

questions.correctAnswerText: Service type is associated with both arrival time and wait time, so the combined negative association should not be interpreted as a common within-type trend.
questions.explanation: Service type acts as a grouping variable connected to both x and y. Aggregating the groups creates an association that is absent within each group.

questions.unit: Unit 2: Probability, Random Variables, and Probability Distributions
questions.prompt: A continuous probability density has height 1.5 over part of its support. Which statement is correct?

choices.A: A density height can exceed 1 because probabilities are areas under the curve, and the total area must equal 1.
choices.B: The model is invalid because every density height must be at most 1.
choices.C: The probability of any exact value in that region is 1.5.
choices.D: The total area under the density must equal its maximum height.

questions.correctAnswerText: A density height can exceed 1 because probabilities are areas under the curve, and the total area must equal 1.
questions.explanation: Density is probability per unit on the horizontal scale, not point probability. A curve may exceed height 1 over a sufficiently narrow interval while retaining total area 1.

questions.unit: Unit 3: Inference for Categorical Data: Proportions
questions.prompt: A 95% confidence interval for p₁ − p₂ is (−0.01, 0.01). Before seeing the data, differences within ±0.03 were defined as practically negligible. Which interpretation is best?

choices.A: The interval proves p₁ = p₂ exactly.
choices.B: The interval shows a statistically significant nonzero difference.
choices.C: The practical threshold must be reduced to ±0.01 after seeing the data.
choices.D: Although exact equality is not proved, all values in the interval are within the prespecified range of practical similarity.

questions.correctAnswerText: Although exact equality is not proved, all values in the interval are within the prespecified range of practical similarity.
questions.explanation: The interval includes zero, so it does not establish a nonzero difference, but its entire range lies inside the predeclared negligible band from −0.03 to 0.03. This supports practical similarity without proving exact equality.

questions.unit: Unit 1: Exploring One-Variable Data and Collecting Data
questions.prompt: A bar chart compares proportions 0.48 and 0.52 but uses a vertical axis from 0.45 to 0.55. Which assessment is most appropriate?

choices.A: The actual difference is 40 percentage points because the bars fill 40% of the displayed axis.
choices.B: The actual difference is 4 percentage points, and the truncated axis can visually exaggerate it.
choices.C: The two proportions are equal because both are near 0.50.
choices.D: A bar chart must always begin at the smaller observed proportion.

questions.correctAnswerText: The actual difference is 4 percentage points, and the truncated axis can visually exaggerate it.
questions.explanation: The numerical difference is 0.52 − 0.48 = 0.04, or 4 percentage points. Beginning the axis at 0.45 magnifies the visual height difference.

questions.unit: Unit 1: Exploring One-Variable Data and Collecting Data
questions.prompt: Researchers classify animal behavior from video and want to assess measurement reliability. Which plan is best?

choices.A: Have one rater recode only the clips that were difficult.
choices.B: Tell a second rater the first rater's classifications before recoding.
choices.C: Randomly select a subset of clips and have two trained raters independently classify them while blinded to each other's decisions.
choices.D: Use two raters on different species and compare their overall percentages.

questions.correctAnswerText: Randomly select a subset of clips and have two trained raters independently classify them while blinded to each other's decisions.
questions.explanation: Independent blinded ratings of the same randomly selected clips permit direct assessment of agreement without one rater influencing the other.

questions.unit: Unit 1: Exploring One-Variable Data and Collecting Data
questions.prompt: Nine positive lengths have median 4 centimeters. Each length is transformed to the area of a square with that side length, y = x². What is the median of the nine transformed values?

choices.A: 2 square centimeters
choices.B: 4 square centimeters
choices.C: 8 square centimeters
choices.D: 16 square centimeters

questions.correctAnswerText: 16 square centimeters
questions.explanation: Squaring is strictly increasing for positive values, so it preserves their order. The original middle value 4 therefore remains the middle observation after transformation and becomes 4² = 16 square centimeters.
